item.text: I’m moving into `com.google.common.collect` now and will look for the same kind of repeated branching or helper duplication that was cleaned up in `base`. I’ll keep the changes conservative and mirrored across the JRE and Android trees.

I’m checking the smaller collect-side helpers first. `CollectPreconditions` is the most obvious analogue to the `base` cleanup, and I’m also sampling a couple of adjacent utilities to avoid picking an outlier.

I found a good low-risk duplication in `Comparators`: `isInOrder` and `isInStrictOrder` are the same loop with one comparison flip. I’m also checking whether `CollectPreconditions` is worth a matching helper extraction, since it’s the other small collect-side utility with repeated exception construction.

I’ve got two targeted collect-side cleanups lined up: one in `CollectPreconditions` to factor repeated exception creation, and one in `Comparators` to collapse the duplicated order-checking loop into a shared helper.
The refactors are applied. I’m validating formatting and recompilation now, then I’ll summarize exactly what changed in the collect package.
